checks: In a closed irreducible class every base coordinate is harmonic. Its maximum propagates to every positive-probability successor and then throughout the class. Distinct bases make such a class a singleton, and a chosen row leaves its starting state with positive probability, ruling out closed chosen singletons.

The communicating-class graph is finite and acyclic. A positive-probability path to a terminal exists from each state, including when the initial state is already terminal. Finiteness gives a uniform finite block length and positive lower hitting probability. Iterating the Markov property yields almost-sure finite absorption.

The bounded coordinate martingales converge to the terminal coordinates, so bounded convergence gives the stated expectations for base and lift. The upper support equality propagates at each positive transition by harmonicity and nonnegativity of the affine gap.
